english.notes:
(i) This offence may be considered where one person offers to make some purported intimate images of a person in general, and another person replies with a request for a specific image, such as an image of that person in particular underwear, naked or engaged in a particular sexual act.
(ii) Making a "request" includes both making a request directed to a particular person or persons, and making a request available to one or more people (or people generally), without directing it to a particular person or people (for example, by posting a request on a large online forum) (section 66F(4)).
(iii) A ‘request’ includes doing an act which could reasonably be taken to be a request (nodding, giving a ‘thumbs up’, ‘liking’ a message or otherwise indicating agreement in response to an offer, or complying with condition of an offer, for example by sending money) (section 66F(3)).
(iv) The offence can be committed irrespective of whether or not the image being requested is ever, in fact, created and irrespective of whether another individual has also made the same request for a purported intimate image (section 66F(6)).
(v) Subsection 66F(7) provides for a defence of reasonable excuse, with the legal burden on the defendant. Where a defendant can prove on the balance of probabilities, they had a reasonable excuse for requesting the creation of the image, they would not be guilty of the offence. The Government anticipates application only in very rare scenarios where there is a genuinely reasonable, not spurious, excuse. The bar will be especially high for images appearing to show a person engaged in sexual activity. For example, if a person created a purported intimate image but claimed it was a legitimate work of satire, it is extremely unlikely that they would be able to satisfy the legal burden of proving that there was a reasonable excuse.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 66H

The penalty for this offence is based on the maximum term for summary offences. In relation to an offence committed before section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the maximum term is 6 months. Where an offence is committed after that time, it is 51 weeks.
